title: The Trampoline TCO Evaluator: Converting Recursion to Iteration
description: A tail-call-optimized Scheme evaluator using a while True loop. Tail positions (if branches, begin last expr, let body, procedure calls) rewrite x and env then continue instead of recursing.
source: draft: opencode free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Thunk class wraps a zero-argument callable. trampoline repeatedly calls val() while val is a Thunk, returning the final value. This is the classic trampoline pattern.

scheme_eval_tco inlines the trampoline: instead of returning Thunks, tail positions update x and env then continue the while True loop. The function is called via trampoline(scheme_eval_tco(expr, env)).
The while True loop starts. Atoms (numbers, booleans, strings) return immediately. Symbols look up via env.find. Non-lists or empty lists raise error.

if special form: test is evaluated with trampoline (not tail). The chosen branch becomes the new x, and continue restarts the loop  -  this is the tail position. The alternate branch is never evaluated.
define: for (define (name params) body) creates ProcedureTCO directly. For (define name value), value is evaluated with trampoline then bound in current env. Returns None.

steps.question: In the begin form (lines 61-66), all but the last expression are evaluated with trampoline, but the last expression does `x = x[-1]; continue`. Why is only the last expression in tail position?
steps.answer: In (begin e1 e2 e3), e1 and e2 are evaluated for side effects only  -  their values are discarded. After e1 returns, we must evaluate e2. After e2 returns, we must evaluate e3. Only after e3 returns does begin finish, so e3 is in tail position. The loop evaluates e1..e(n-1) via trampoline (discarding results), then sets x to the last expr and continues.

steps.description: let desugars to a lambda call: params and args are evaluated (args with trampoline). A new env is created with those bindings. x becomes the body, and continue loops; the body is in tail position.

Procedure call: head and all args are evaluated with trampoline. If proc is ProcedureTCO, a new call env is created with proc.params, args, and proc.env (lexical). x becomes proc.body, continue loops  -  the call is in tail position. Primitive procs (callable) are called directly and return.
ProcedureTCO stores params, body, env. No __call__ method  -  the evaluator handles calling directly in the tail-call branch.
Run it. Demo 1: count-down defined. run() parses and evaluates with trampoline(scheme_eval_tco(...)).
(count-down 100000): each tail call updates x=body, env=call_env, continues. 100000 iterations, constant Python stack. Returns 0. Prints 'count-down 100000 => 0'.
Demo 2: sum-iter tail-recursive sum with accumulator. (sum-iter 1000 0) adds the values from 1000 down to 1. Tail calls loop without stack growth. Prints the sum.
